purpose: Every subject's KOS/Qified paper tests significant direct, downstream and long-tail consequences only when credible relevance and evidence exist. SHOCK is cross-cutting, not a policing subsection.

eventTypes.title: Electricity outage or grid constraint
eventTypes.mechanism: A sudden or sustained loss of electric service can interrupt water pumping, heating, healthcare, refrigeration, communications and businesses.

eventTypes.title: Fuel, natural gas or heating shortage
eventTypes.mechanism: Fuel and gas disruptions can interrupt transportation, household heating, generators, manufacturing and emergency response.

eventTypes.title: Water supply, treatment or contamination event
eventTypes.mechanism: Supply, treatment, pipeline or water-quality problems can affect drinking water, hospitals, schools, businesses and irrigation.

eventTypes.title: Sewer or wastewater failure
eventTypes.mechanism: Treatment failures, overflows and infrastructure damage can affect public health, waterways, businesses and cleanup costs.

eventTypes.title: Drought and water scarcity
eventTypes.mechanism: Long-running water shortages can affect households, agriculture, industry, utilities, wildfire risk and regional agreements.

eventTypes.title: Flood, storm, snow, extreme heat or cold
eventTypes.mechanism: Severe conditions can close roads, damage homes and public assets, interrupt energy and endanger vulnerable residents.

eventTypes.title: Wildfire and smoke
eventTypes.mechanism: Fire and smoke can threaten homes, forests, public health, tourism, emergency capacity and water quality.

eventTypes.title: Cyberattack, ransomware or malicious intrusion
eventTypes.mechanism: Attacks on utilities, hospitals, schools, firms or government can interrupt services, payments, operations and data access.

eventTypes.title: 911, dispatch, broadband or communications outage
eventTypes.mechanism: Loss of communications can delay emergency response, public warnings, education, commerce and public services.

eventTypes.title: Banking, payment or data-system failure
eventTypes.mechanism: Payment, identity or records disruption can affect payroll, benefits, taxes, commerce and access to essential services.

eventTypes.title: Food shortage or distribution disruption
eventTypes.mechanism: Crop losses, transport problems or sudden cost pressures can reduce access to food, including for children and older adults.

eventTypes.title: Infectious disease outbreak or public-health surge
eventTypes.mechanism: Disease events can strain healthcare, schools, workplaces, caregiving and essential-service staffing.

eventTypes.title: Hospital, EMS, medication or medical-supply disruption
eventTypes.mechanism: A care-capacity failure or medicine shortage can block treatment, emergency response and continuing support.

eventTypes.title: Strike, labor stoppage or major staffing shortage
eventTypes.mechanism: A lawful strike or staffing shortage can affect service delivery and supply chains; distinguish labor rights from actual service consequences.

eventTypes.title: Supply-chain or essential-material shortage
eventTypes.mechanism: Missing equipment, inputs, construction materials, medication or parts can delay essential repairs and operations.

eventTypes.title: Transport corridor closure or hazardous-material event
eventTypes.mechanism: Road, rail, airport or hazardous-cargo events can disrupt mobility, commerce and public health.

eventTypes.title: Industrial accident, explosion or hazardous release
eventTypes.mechanism: A production failure, fire or release may affect workers, air and water, transport and nearby communities.

eventTypes.title: Sudden housing displacement or shelter shortage
eventTypes.mechanism: An emergency, eviction wave or facility closure can displace residents and overwhelm food, health and shelter services.

eventTypes.title: Funding cut, delayed grant or fiscal-service crisis
eventTypes.mechanism: Funding interruptions can affect workers, nonprofits, healthcare, education, infrastructure and essential services.

eventTypes.title: Major legal, regulatory or jurisdictional change
eventTypes.mechanism: A verified new requirement or decision can change benefits, operating duties, public spending and compliance deadlines.

eventTypes.title: School, childcare or youth-service disruption
eventTypes.mechanism: Closures, staffing shortfalls or system failures can affect learning, family employment, meals and care.

eventTypes.title: False emergency information or critical public-notice failure
eventTypes.mechanism: Conflicting, false or missing notices can prevent informed protective action and damage trust.

eventTypes.title: AI, automated-control or data-integrity failure
eventTypes.mechanism: A flawed automated process can disrupt decisions, deny needed services or produce unsafe recommendations; humans retain authority.

eventTypes.title: Environmental damage, crop disease or ecosystem disruption
eventTypes.mechanism: Contamination, plant/animal disease or habitat damage can affect food, water, tourism, farms and long-term restoration.

eventTypes.title: Community-service overload or assistance network interruption
eventTypes.mechanism: Loss or overload of shelters, food programs, caregivers and support networks can leave essential needs unmet.

recognitionRules.notEveryChangeIsShock: A scheduled repair, budget proposal or peaceful labor action is not an emergency by itself; look for documented essential-service interruption, credible imminent threat or severe actual consequence.
recognitionRules.sourceRequirement: Show authority, original public source URL, incident/event time, geographic scope, last verified date, review due and corrections; no invented current alerts.
analyticalSequence: Check source and actual vs hypothetical status
Crosswalk the affected people, entities, assets, services and funding
Trace immediate, secondary and longer-term effects
Evaluate human protection and independent backups
Compare realistic mitigations, costs and tradeoffs
Explain it in the KOS paper; elevate only verified current high-impact events to What's Happening Now
recognitionRules.sourceProtocol: Q Pueblo is not an emergency notification authority; official and authorized warning sources govern protective action and immediacy. A Q analysis does not itself make a public safety determination.
recognitionRules.publicationGate: Public alerts require human editorial verification and appropriate official attribution. No unattended event generation or publishing.
